title: Trace context annotation standard for LLM microcalls
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight, pragmatic standard for trace/span attribute names and sampling hooks specific to LLM microcall topologies (router -> batcher -> model shards -> kernel -> postprocess). Aim: consistent, searchable attributes that make cross-tenant/blame investigations fast, and that enable compact dashboards and deterministic sampling rules for high-value traces (fallbacks, regressions, high-cost).

Background / motivation:
- Our existing traces are inconsistent: similar events use different attribute keys across services (e.g., `tenant` vs `customer.id`), which makes queries and dashboards brittle.
- LLM inference has many microcalls and compact spans (kernel steps, kv cache hits, routing decisions). We need minimal, high-signal attributes per span to trace cost + quality regressions quickly.
- Sampling budgets are finite; we should prioritize traces that reveal high unit cost, fallbacks, or quality alerts.

High-level conventions (apply everywhere):
- Attribute namespace: all custom attributes MUST be prefixed with `rw.` (short for Redwood). Examples: `rw.tenant_id`, `rw.model.id`.
- Sensitive values: do NOT put PII in attributes. Tenant IDs should be hashed using the platform tenant-hash (sha256 prefix) and stored as `rw.tenant_hash` when required.
- Consistent types: counters and durations use suffix `_ms` for milliseconds or `_count` for integers. Booleans use `_flag`.
- Span naming: use dot-separated verbs: `request.root`, `router.route`, `batcher.create_batch`, `serve.infer`, `kernel.exec`, `cache.lookup`, `postprocess.render`.

Required root/span attributes (minimum set) - root span (request.root):
- rw.request_id: (string) platform request uuid (trace id may be used but keep explicit)
- rw.tenant_hash: (string) hashed tenant id
- rw.route_key: (string) logical route name from config (e.g., `chat.v1-small`)
- rw.model_id: (string) canonical model id used for inference (e.g., `openlm/llama-3-13b-q`)
- rw.model_variant: (string) user-visible variant tag or quantization profile (e.g., `q4f16-slim`)
- rw.total_tokens_in: (int)_count (input tokens counted by tokenizer)
- rw.tokens_generated: (int)_count (0 if streaming not yet produced)
- rw.client_region: (string) client region or region hint
- rw.fallback_flag: (bool) true if any fallback path was taken

Span-level common attributes (applies to sub-spans):
- rw.span_index: (int)_count (consecutive integer for microcall ordering in same trace)
- rw.batch_id: (string) id of batch when batching used
- rw.queue_time_ms: (int)_ms (time waiting in batch queue)
- rw.exec_time_ms: (int)_ms (execution kernel time)
- rw.kv_hit_flag: (bool) true if KV/prefix cache returned a hit
- rw.cache_tier: (string) e.g., `local`, `regional`, `global`

Special attributes for routing/fallback spans:
- rw.routing_policy: (string) e.g., `latency-prefer`, `cost-prefer`, `tiered-fallback`
- rw.fallback_reason: (string) canonical tag for why fallback happened: `capacity`, `timeout`, `latency_slo`, `model_error`, `quality_regression`
- rw.fallback_from: (string) model id that was attempted
- rw.fallback_to: (string) model id used as fallback

Attributes for kernel/exec spans (for perf attribution):
- rw.kernel_name: (string) kernel implementation id
- rw.seq_len_in: (int)_count (seq length for this microcall)
- rw.max_gpu_mem_mb: (int)_count
- rw.quant_profile: (string) e.g., `int8-ggml`, `q4_k_mixed`
- rw.cuda_stream_ms: (int)_ms (time spent in CUDA streams if available)

Quality telemetry hints (trace-level flags we want to surface for evaluations):
- rw.eval_prompt_id: (string) optional id for a known test/prompt used during telemetry reruns
- rw.hallucination_flag: (bool) if downstream quality signal flagged hallucination (populated by eval tooling)
- rw.quality_regression_score: (int)_count (relative score change when available)

Sampling strategy / budget rules (practical):
- Global base sample rate: 1% of traces, low-overhead preserves headroom.
- Always sample full traces if any of these are true: rw.fallback_flag == true, HTTP >= 5xx, rw.hallucination_flag == true, rw.quality_regression_score > 0, rw.exec_time_ms > 2000ms, rw.tokens_generated > 2048.
- Adaptive spike sampling: if we detect > 3x baseline P95 latency for a model in last 1m, temporarily increase sampling for that model to 20% for 10m.
- Cost-focused sampling: periodically (hourly) sample a small fraction (0.5%) of traces weighted by estimated token-cost = rw.tokens_generated + rw.total_tokens_in * model_cost_factor to catch expensive outliers.
- Low-cardinality trace skeletons: for high-volume low-latency requests (<50ms p95), store span aggregates and only sample full traces for a tiny fraction (0.1%) to reduce ingestion.

Dashboard and alert mapping (minimal widgets):
- Model cost heatmap: columns=hour, rows=model_variant, color=mean cost-per-request (tokens*model-cost). Drilldown link to sampled traces filtered to top 10 expensive traces.
- Fallback timeline: stacked area of `fallback_from` per hour with `fallback_reason` legend. Annotate deploy/rollback windows.
- Latency waterfall by span: widget that shows p50/p95/p99 for rw.queue_time_ms, rw.exec_time_ms, postprocess time.
- Trace-count-by-sampling-rule: shows which sampling rule captured traces to validate coverage.
- Quality signal correlation: overlay of `rw.hallucination_flag` rate vs model variant traffic.

Suggested SLI / SLOs (examples to bake into product-level dashboards):
- Inference availability: fraction of requests that returned 2xx within 10s. (SLO: 99.9% monthly)
- P95 inference latency (end-to-end) per model variant (SLOs vary by tier, e.g., <600ms for tier-1 models).
- Fallback rate: fraction of requests that hit fallback for a model (SLA guidance: <0.5% for dedicated pools).
- Cost-per-1000-tokens trending for billing and anomaly detection.

Investigation playbook (short):
1) Confirm user report / synthetic probe: get rw.request_id or time window and tenant_hash.
2) Check fallback timeline dashboard for this model/tenant at the reported time.
3) Query sampled traces for rw.request_id or rw.tenant_hash in a 2m window; if none, look at sampled aggregates and bump sampling for that model (temporary).
4) Inspect root trace attributes: rw.fallback_flag, rw.fallback_reason, rw.routing_policy.
5) Drill into spans: look at `rw.queue_time_ms` spikes vs `rw.exec_time_ms` to decide if we hit queuing or kernel issues.
6) If exec_time_ms high: check `rw.kernel_name`, `rw.seq_len_in`, and `rw.quant_profile`. Correlate with recent kernel PRs (check linked PRs).
7) If fallback due to capacity: check Dedicated pool metrics and autoscaler events (link to capacity dashboard).
8) If hallucination/quality: pull eval prompt via rw.eval_prompt_id and run locally to reproduce.

Examples (human-readable traces):
- Short successful trace:
  request.root rw.request_id=abc123, rw.tenant_hash=tx1, rw.route_key=chat.v1, rw.model_id=llama-3-7b, rw.tokens_generated=45
  router.route rw.span_index=1 rw.routing_policy=latency-prefer
  batcher.create_batch rw.span_index=2 rw.batch_id=b-998 rw.queue_time_ms=12
  serve.infer rw.span_index=3 rw.exec_time_ms=78 rw.kernel_name=k-v2
  postprocess.render rw.span_index=4 rw.exec_time_ms=10

- Fallback trace where fallback to smaller model happened:
  request.root rw.fallback_flag=true rw.fallback_reason=capacity rw.fallback_from=llama-3-13b rw.fallback_to=llama-3-7b

Open questions / TODOs (treat as living list):
- Should `rw.model_variant` include a hashed component to avoid leaking exact infra details for regulated customers? (Sana to confirm with security)
- Define canonical list of `rw.fallback_reason` enums and map them to alert severities (Diego).
- Decide whether to include pre-tokenization input size or raw byte-size; tokenizer-based tokens preferred but not always available.
- Standardize how SDKs populate rw.* attributes (client SDKs vs internal proxies). Ownership: platform-instrumentation team.

Migration notes / compatibility:
- Backfill plan: for the first rollout, populate rw.* attributes in new services and add a compatibility layer that maps legacy keys (`tenant`, `model`) into rw.* for dashboards during transition.
- Query templates: attach sample queries to the confluence page (linked artifact) for common debug flows.

Appendix: quick attribute index (flat list):
rw.request_id, rw.tenant_hash, rw.route_key, rw.model_id, rw.model_variant, rw.total_tokens_in, rw.tokens_generated, rw.client_region, rw.fallback_flag, rw.fallback_reason, rw.fallback_from, rw.fallback_to, rw.routing_policy, rw.span_index, rw.batch_id, rw.queue_time_ms, rw.exec_time_ms, rw.kv_hit_flag, rw.cache_tier, rw.kernel_name, rw.seq_len_in, rw.max_gpu_mem_mb, rw.quant_profile, rw.cuda_stream_ms, rw.eval_prompt_id, rw.hallucination_flag, rw.quality_regression_score

If you are reviewing: please comment inline on the confluence copy (link above) and add any missing enum values for fallback_reason. I want this to be lightweight and enforceable within the next sprint - aim to land instrumentation shims in the runtime + proxy and then roll dashboards to the canonical names.

Planner notes (internal):
- Owner: Marcus Chen (eng-observability)
- Immediate next steps: PR for instrumentation shim (github PR linked), one small canary service to adopt rw.* for 2 weeks, run comparative queries to validate coverage, then wider rollout.

Notes to self (rough):
- keep attribute list short. Resist adding more than 3-4 model-specific keys unless we have a real use-case.
- follow up with security on tenant hashing approach.
